audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer explains how Yasuo actually lands Last Breath. mid says 'he can Sweeping-Blade in and ult you off your own knockup', which is backwards, and dontsFull[0] says Last Breath 'catches you mid-dash'.
audit.why: Last Breath only blinks to an AIRBORNE enemy champion. Galio's own knockups land on Yasuo, not on Galio, so they cannot feed it, and being mid-dash is not airborne. The knockup that enables his ultimate is his own: Steel Tempest builds Gathering Storm and at 2 stacks fires a whirlwind that knocks you airborne, on a 4-second base cooldown. So the real kill chain is Q-Q whirlwind into R, and the tell is the second Steel Tempest — not his dash and not your own E.
audit.corrected: Last Breath needs you airborne, and the only thing that puts you there is his own second Steel Tempest whirlwind. Count his Q stacks: the second one is the ult setup, and Justice Punch mid-flight does not make you a target.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (Q Steel Tempest: 'At 2 stacks, Steel Tempest fires a whirlwind that knocks Airborne', cooldown 4, flags knockup; R Last Breath: 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion', 70/50/30)
champ-data/_kits/galio.json (E Justice Punch knocks up the enemy, not Galio)

audit.why: The entry's central interaction is right and well stated: Wind Wall blocks the Winds of War windblasts but not the Shield of Durand taunt or the Justice Punch dash, so you commit through the wall instead of poking into it. The wiki confirms Wind Wall blocks each windblast individually and that neither W nor E is a projectile. This is the best line on the page and I left it intact, only adding the 25-second cooldown so a player can count it.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio (Winds of War: 'Yasuo's Wind Wall and Braum's Unbreakable can block each windblast individually'; W and E are not projectiles)
champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (W Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17, blocks all enemy projectiles for 4s)

audit.whatIsWrong: Every cooldown reference is 'when Last Breath is down' in tldr, winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], report[5] and report[9] — with no number anywhere, and Wind Wall's cooldown never given despite being the ability that shuts off Galio's poke.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17 for a 4-second wall, so a spent wall gives you roughly 21 seconds of free Winds of War at rank 1 — the single most useful clock in the lane. Last Breath is 70/50/30, Steel Tempest is a 4-second base, and Sweeping Blade is effectively off cooldown but cannot be re-cast on the same target for a few seconds, which is why he needs the wave to keep dashing.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall 25s at rank 1 for a 4-second wall — poke freely in the 21 seconds after. Last Breath 70s at rank 1. Steel Tempest 4s base. Sweeping Blade has no real cooldown but cannot re-target you immediately.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (W 25/23/21/19/17; R 70/50/30; Q 4; E 0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1, 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds')

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why says 'the dash is interruptible and root-able mid-flight'.
audit.why: Justice Punch cannot be interrupted once travelling, and Yasuo has no root. His only crowd control is the Steel Tempest whirlwind knockup and the hold on Last Breath. Naming a root he does not have crowds out the knockup he does.
audit.corrected: Yasuo has no root. The only thing that stops your combo is the Steel Tempest whirlwind knockup at 2 stacks, which also cancels a charging Shield of Durand.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio (Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel)
champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (no root; Q knockup at 2 stacks)

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr says 'Your MR shield blanks him' and report[0] repeats it.
audit.why: Yasuo is a physical-damage champion — the entry's own late line says so ('Shield of Durand's magic-damage amp is dead weight against a pure-AD champion'). Shield of Durand cuts physical only 12.5% at rank 1 against 25% versus magic. The headline and the closing paragraph of the same page say opposite things about the same button.
audit.corrected: The stance is not the reason you win this lane — against physical it stops only 12.5% at rank 1. The taunt is the reason, plus a Wind Wall that cannot block it.
sources: champ-data/content/galio.js (late: 'dead weight against a pure-AD champion')

audit.whatIsWrong: Way of the Wanderer is never mentioned.
audit.why: Yasuo builds a shield whenever he is moving, and it triggers on the first champion damage he takes. Against a Galio whose plan is one big taunt-and-punch burst, that shield is the first thing your combo spends itself on — which is a concrete argument for opening with a Winds of War tick to pop it before the taunt lands.
audit.corrected: Way of the Wanderer builds a shield while he moves and pops on the first champion damage — chip it off with a Q tick before you spend the taunt combo into it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (P Way of the Wanderer: 'builds toward a shield whenever he is moving. The shield triggers when he takes damage from a champion or monster', flags shield)

notes: The kill chain against Galio is Steel Tempest to two Gathering Storm stacks, whirlwind knockup, then Last Breath — Galio's own Justice Punch and Hero's Entrance knockups land on the enemy and cannot feed a Yasuo ultimate, so the previous 'he ults you off your own knockup' framing was inverted. Galio facts verified at wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio and reused across this slice: Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% and physical exactly half (12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%), passive magic shield 7.5/9/10.5/12/13.5% max health restoring after 12/10/8s untouched. Justice Punch knocks up 0.75s, cannot be interrupted mid-travel, disabled while Grounded, halts on terrain or champions. Winds of War 825 with a 2-second tornado and no slow; Wind Wall and Braum's Unbreakable block each windblast individually, and a spell shield eats the gusts but not the tornado. Hero's Entrance channels 2.75s, CC-immune after 1.25s. Colossal Smash is a 5s empowered auto scaling with 60% bonus MR.
